_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform. The ✳️any subset registers `lopdf` under `pdf-1-7-mutate` for the DOCUMENT vocabulary; this file registers the same package under a distinct id and the `pdf-1-7-vt-mutate` capability the CONFORMANCE-CLASS case (`mutate-pdf-1-7-vt`) tags, because reusing a neighbour's entry fails the contract with `oracle-capability-mismatch`.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED, on the same ground as `gltf`, `png`, `jpg`, `bmp`, `tiff` and `avi`. `lopdf` is a real PDF codec and does real work — but what a MUTATION SHOULD PRODUCE is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs`, whose doc comments say it plainly: the forward and undo results are "read out of the BYTES by the INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION". The fixtures registered alongside are generated through that same second implementation (`apply_conformance_mutation` in `semio-s-plugin-stdio-test-oracle`), so both halves of the comparison descend from one reading of the specification, and a misreading of it yields two agreeing wrong answers.

`lopdf` discharges "the result is a well-formed PDF", NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for. A required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute.

The fixtures stay and are valuable: real PDF bytes, byte-reproducible, covering every declared kind of this conformance profile — exactly what a qualifying third-party reference gets pointed at when one exists.

📖️ A READER — and the reason this subset needed one is worth stating exactly, because the sibling entry looked qualifying and was not.

The previous fixture corpus was generated by a binary that imported `oracle_apply_mutation` and `project_conformance` from `semio-s-plugin-stdio-test-oracle`, this repository's OWN crate. The mutated bytes and the expected projection of them were therefore both ours, and `lopdf` was reduced to a codec for our own answer: a shared misreading of the PDF specification would have produced two agreeing wrong answers and the test would still have passed. Registering a reader beside that corpus would have changed the label and nothing else.

So the corpus was REBUILT. `🦀️lopdf-engine` depends on `lopdf` and nothing else: it lays out the seed, performs each mutation through lopdf's own public COS API, and reads the conformance axes back through it. Nothing in this repository predicts what this reader judges.

Two of the eighteen kinds are registered `-uncarried` rather than routed around: lopdf 0.44's writer takes its encryption path whenever the trailer carries `/Encrypt` and then requires the encryption state a genuine decryption would have recorded, so a synthetic encryption dictionary can be neither written nor read back. That is a writer-side limit, not a reader gap.

📖️ A SECOND reader for the two kinds `lopdf` can neither write nor read.

Both halves were measured. WRITING: lopdf 0.44's writer takes its encryption path whenever the trailer carries `/Encrypt` and then requires the encryption state a genuine decryption would have recorded, so a synthetic encryption dictionary fails on its own output (`object ID 8 0 not found`). READING: handed a genuinely encrypted PDF, lopdf DECRYPTS transparently with the empty user password and then reports `is_encrypted() == false` — so even a real encrypted fixture would project as unencrypted. That is why these two kinds were `-uncarried`, and it was a statement about lopdf, not about PDF libraries.

pypdf 6.14 does both: `PdfWriter.encrypt` emits a real standard security handler, and `PdfReader.is_encrypted` reports it. Its output is byte-DETERMINISTIC — checked three times before it was relied on, which matters because encryption schemes commonly randomise a key and a non-reproducible fixture would fail this repository's own reproducibility gate.

The reader is shared by all four conformance subsets: the question is identical across them and the framework already lets a probe's `command` point at another subset's script.

comparisonProfiles.description: A PDF document compared by the CONFORMANCE-CLASS surface check_vt_conformance actually reads, every field read back out of the bytes by the independent `lopdf` object-graph reader: the page count as a stability anchor, plus every Standard Security Handler dictionary object, by its /V and /R; every intent reachable from /Root/OutputIntents, by /S marker, output condition identifier and whether it carries a /DestOutputProfile; every page's /TrimBox and /ArtBox; every /Type /FontDescriptor in object-number order, by which of /FontFile, /FontFile2 or /FontFile3 carries its embedded program, how many bytes that program is once its stream filters are DECODED, and a digest of those decoded bytes; every /S /JavaScript action, by the script its /JS carries; every /S /Launch action, by the target its /F carries; every /Subtype /Movie or /Sound annotation, by subtype and title; the /DPartRoot node chain, per node whether it carries /DPM and what that metadata's /Job says. Page CONTENT is deliberately absent — media boxes, content streams and shown text belong to the ✳️any subset's own semantic-pdf-v1 profile, and a conformance class says nothing about them. Object NUMBERS are deliberately absent too: a class is defined on what the document contains, not on where a writer put it, so re-inserting a removed construct at a fresh number is a faithful undo and recording the number would report a false divergence for it. An embedded font program is measured DECODED and never by the length of the stream that stores it: /FontFile, /FontFile2 and /FontFile3 streams are almost always /FlateDecode, and deflate output length is ENCODER FREEDOM — two conformant writers may compress a byte-identical program to byte counts that differ by a byte or two, which is precisely what the first full differential run of these six classes measured (all 23 embedded programs of the real thesis decoded byte-identically while five of their stored streams differed by 1–2 bytes). The ✳️any subset's semantic-pdf-v1 profile already takes that reading, listing streamLength as writer freedom. Decoding is not a relaxation: the decoded length plus a digest of the decoded bytes is a STRICTER axis than the stored length ever was, because a program whose bytes change is now caught even when its length does not. The only numeric fields are the encryption /V and /R, an embedded font program's decoded byte length and the page-box coordinates, all of them exact integers or literal coordinates a writer must reproduce exactly; hence no tolerance.
Whether the document carries a standard security handler, the handler's algorithm, and the page count read after decrypting with the empty user password so both sides of a pair stay comparable.

fixtureManifests.notes: A minimal two-descriptor seed built with lopdf 0.44, with the set-output-intent mutation applied THROUGH lopdf's own public COS API (🦀️lopdf-engine/src/lib.rs::apply) — never through this repository's own mutation engine, which is what made the previous corpus inadmissible as evidence. base.pdf is the seed after 🦀️lopdf-engine's arrange put the mutation's precondition in place (identical to the untouched seed for every kind whose precondition is already satisfied); mutated.pdf is the result lopdf wrote. Observability (mutated projection != base projection, both read back through lopdf) is checked for every pair before it is written, and a pair that does not move is refused rather than committed.

This subset's own committed base document, written twice by pypdf 6.14 — once plain and once with a standard security handler. lopdf, which judges every other kind here, decrypts transparently on load and reports is_encrypted() false on a genuinely encrypted file, and cannot write an encryption dictionary at all. Observability was checked through the pypdf reader before the pair was written.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways for all 16 witnessable kinds, per-fixture: (base,base) -> equal:true for 16/16; (base,mutated) -> equal:false for 16/16 — 32/32 directions correct. Observability is additionally enforced at GENERATION time: 🦀️lopdf-engine refuses to write a pair whose projection does not move, so a no-op mutation cannot be committed as a passing fixture. The two encryption kinds were caught by exactly that check failing to even read its own output (`object ID 8 0 not found`) and are registered -uncarried.

criteria.detail: 16/16 kinds: identical (base,base) compares equal:true
16/16 kinds: the kind's own (base,mutated) compares equal:false
The reader binary projects and compares; it neither applies a mutation nor computes an expected state. The expected state is the committed mutated.pdf.
All 16 pairs regenerate byte-identically (aggregate sha256 unchanged across a full regeneration); no wall-clock and no randomness in the seed
lopdf 0.44.0 is vendored in the cargo registry cache; the crate builds and runs with --offline
